providers.explicit_control_method: prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention parameters on request
providers.ttl_behavior: in_memory: 5-10m idle, max 1h; extended (24h): gpt-5.5+, gpt-5.4+, gpt-4.1. Extended stores KV tensors in GPU-local storage.
providers.disable_method: not_disableable — automatic caching is enabled for all prompts >= 1024 tokens. Extended retention can be opted out by not requesting it.
providers.cache_eviction_behavior: idle_timeout, overflow_routing (>15 req/min per prefix+key combination routes to additional machines)
providers.cost_to_read: up to 90% discount on input tokens
providers.research_notes: OpenAI caching is automatic with no code changes required. The prompt_cache_key and prompt_cache_retention parameters allow explicit routing and retention control. In-memory caches never touch disk. Extended (24h) caches store KV tensors in GPU-local storage — not raw text. ZDR-eligible with in-memory; extended caching is compatible with ZDR for the KV tensor storage. Rig Relay's OpenAI Responses backend extracts cached_tokens from input_tokens_details and maps to LLMUsage.cache_read_tokens. Rig Relay does NOT send prompt_cache_key or prompt_cache_retention parameters. The generic Chat Completions backend also extracts cached_tokens. Cache writes are free — no surcharge. Key risk: confidential repository context placed early in the prompt may be automatically cached and retained as KV tensors for up to 24h on extended retention models.

providers.explicit_control_method: cache_control block on content blocks, or top-level automatic caching on request body
providers.ttl_behavior: 5m default (1.25x base input), 1h opt-in (2x base input). Cache refreshed for no additional cost each time cached content is used.
providers.disable_method: omit_cache_control — simply do not include cache_control blocks or top-level directive
providers.research_notes: Anthropic is the best-supported cache provider in Rig Relay. The Anthropic backend (anrthropic.py) sends cache_control: {type: ephemeral} on system prompt blocks and the last user message block. Beta header prompt-caching-2024-07-31 is included. Both cache_read_input_tokens and cache_creation_input_tokens are fully extracted from streaming and non-streaming responses. The invocation outcome capability matrix marks cache_read_verified=true, cache_creation_verified=true, live_cache_evidence_preserved=true. However: tools are never cached (tools support cache_control, but Rig Relay doesn't use it); only 2 of 4 supported breakpoints are used; the 1h TTL is never used; the top-level automatic caching mode is never used; the newer cache_creation breakdown (ephemeral_5m_input_tokens / ephemeral_1h_input_tokens) is not parsed. Cache retention is in-memory only — KV cache representations and cryptographic hashes are held in memory for the cache TTL and promptly deleted after expiry. As of Feb 2026, cache isolation is per-workspace, not per-organization.

providers.explicit_control_method: client.caches.create() with contents, system_instruction, ttl. Reference via cached_content in GenerateContentConfig.
providers.ttl_behavior: Default 60m for explicit caches. Can set custom TTL (seconds as '3600s' string) at creation or update via client.caches.update(). Can delete explicitly.
providers.disable_method: omit_cache_control — simply do not use explicit caches. Implicit caching behavior from ai.google.dev is not separately documented as disableable.
providers.cost_to_write: standard input token price for cache creation
providers.research_notes: ai.google.dev was unreachable via direct fetch during research (transport errors). Claims cross-validated from Google Gen AI Python SDK (googleapis/python-genai) README and Vertex AI docs, which use the same GenerateContentResponse protobuf schema. The Gemini adapter (gemini.py) reads usageMetadata but only extracts promptTokenCount, candidatesTokenCount, totalTokenCount — it does NOT extract cachedContentTokenCount. No explicit cache creation or management support exists in the Gemini adapter. Cache resource management (create, update, delete) uses the SDK or REST API directly; Rig Relay has no integration. The SDK supports both Gemini API (api_key auth) and Vertex AI (service account auth) with conditional code paths for each. Minimum token threshold not explicitly documented.

providers.explicit_control_method: Implicit: enabled by default, disable via project-level PATCH cacheConfig. Explicit: client.caches.create() with contents, system_instruction, TTL.
providers.ttl_behavior: Implicit: 24h in-memory TTL at project level (not at-rest). Explicit: default 60m, custom TTL at creation or update. Explicit caches incur storage costs; implicit do not.
providers.disable_method: project_level_config — PATCH /v1/projects/{PROJECT}/cacheConfig with disableCache:true. Requires aiplatform.admin role.
providers.cost_to_write: standard input token price for explicit cache creation. No storage cost for implicit. Storage costs for explicit caches based on duration.
providers.cost_to_read: 90% discount on cached tokens (implicit and 2.5+ explicit), 75% discount (2.0 explicit)
providers.research_notes: Vertex AI has the most complex caching model: two types (implicit + explicit) that interact. Implicit caching is enabled by default, provides automatic 90% discount on cache hits, stores Customer Data in-memory with 24h TTL at project level (not at-rest). Explicit caching offers API-controlled cache resources with CRUD operations, custom TTL, and storage costs. Adheres to Data Residency and is ZDR-compatible. Can be disabled project-wide. Explicit caches interact with implicit caching, potentially leading to additional caching beyond specified contents. Vertex AI override via VertexAnthropicAdapter inherits Anthropic caching behavior (cache_control for Claude models), not Gemini caching. The Gemini adapter does not handle caching at all.

DeepSeek's KV Cache API endpoint (api-docs.deepseek.com/guides/kv_cache) is referenced in Rig Relay's deep-research audit documents but was not independently verified during this research. The invocation outcome capability matrix marks cache_read_verified=false, cache_creation_verified=false, live_cache_evidence_preserved=false. No cache extraction code exists in the generic OpenAI-compatible backend used for DeepSeek. The orchestrator model binding does not declare supports_prompt_cache for DeepSeek. Recommendation: research DeepSeek KV Cache before v1 inclusion.

providers.models_or_families: all routed models (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, DeepSeek, Meta, etc.)
providers.explicit_control_method: none — OpenRouter passes through upstream provider behavior but caches may differ from direct provider caches
providers.ttl_behavior: depends on upstream provider and OpenRouter gateway cache behavior. Not independently documented.
providers.disable_method: not_disableable at OpenRouter level. Upstream provider disable methods may not be reachable through OpenRouter.
providers.cache_eviction_behavior: unknown — depends on gateway cache policy and upstream provider behavior
providers.cost_to_read: depends on upstream provider and OpenRouter pricing model
providers.research_notes: OpenRouter is a gateway — caching behavior depends on the upstream provider being routed to. The generic backend extracts cached_tokens from prompt_tokens_details when present. OpenRouter observer (openrouter_observer.py) normalizes cached_tokens in rich usage. However, the cache that serves the tokens may be OpenRouter's gateway cache, the upstream provider's cache, or both — Rig Relay cannot distinguish. Cache write tokens are never reported. The invocation outcome marks cache_read_verified=true but cache_creation_verified=false. Key risk: transparent provider routing means the user cannot know which provider's retention policy applies to cached content.

providers.models_or_families: Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp, local model servers
providers.explicit_control_method: local OMLX KV cache is managed locally within the inference process. Rig Relay controls data retention through the retention policy (retention_policy.py).
providers.ttl_behavior: Configurable via RawRetentionPolicy: ttl_seconds=0 (disabled), 3600 (raw_local_ttl), 7200 (raw_local_debug_packet). Default: disabled.
providers.disable_method: retention_policy ttl_seconds=0 disables local raw transcript retention. In-process KV cache is ephemeral to the model runtime.
providers.research_notes: Local inference retention is modeled separately from cloud provider caching, per the doctrine requirement. The retention policy (providers/local_inference/retention_policy.py) manages local raw transcript storage with configurable TTL. The in-process KV cache used by local model runtimes (Ollama, llama.cpp, etc.) is an ephemeral GPU data structure that lives only for the duration of the inference session — it is not analogous to cloud provider prompt caching and does not represent a data retention risk. No cache usage fields are extracted because local inference does not expose them in a standardized format. Local inference is always privacy-safe — data never leaves the machine. The retention policy with ttl_seconds=0 provides the strongest local privacy guarantee.
